about: T7's real documents (t7.py, mkreal.py; lane REAL-DOC-GATE 2026-10-24). target_ms: DESIGN.md 1.2, slowest supported Mac, key -> preview commit <= 20 ms p95 for keys 50 ms apart on 1,000-page documents and Infinite Descent x2. pages: the oracle's (pdflatex, TeX Live 2026, passes until the count is stable). A site's page is 0-based and only steers dl3-keys' search for a prose line of its edit file (the nearest one is taken); line + page (beamer) are exact, from the oracle's SyncTeX for the frame's \end{frame} line.

pr_gate.about: t7.py --gate hosted, the PR CI's real-doc-gate (Commander 2026-10-24: wall-clock ms on a shared 3-vCPU VM is noise). A letter@ key passes when the host re-typesets at most rerun_pages_max pages (DONE rerun_pages: it converged next to the edit) and spends at most edited_instr_m_max million engine-thread instructions to the edited page (DONE stages.edited_instr_k: load and clock speed do not move it); a typing@ key when it is painted by its own compile. The budget (derived, not measured on an M1): DESIGN 1.2's 20 ms on the slowest supported Mac at about 5 G instructions/s; this engine's x2-late edit path retires 9.2 G/s on an M5 Pro (median of 6 keys, 2026-10-24), and an M1 core is about 1.75x slower (Geekbench 6 single-core), so 20 ms is about 100 M. Main spends 207 M per key there and re-typesets 266 pages.
